Class PeeringIntelligence

java.lang.Object
com.eqixiac.equinix.design.peering.PeeringIntelligence
public class PeeringIntelligence extends Object
Entry point for Peering Intelligence — an interconnection analysis tool that combines PeeringDB IX peering data with Equinix Fabric private connectivity data to produce unified presence matrices, resiliency assessments, and peering opportunity discovery.

Capabilities

  • Presence Matrix: ASN x Metro grid showing IX peering, Fabric availability, port capacity, and route server participation at every Equinix location
  • Resiliency Analysis: Blast radius evaluation, correlated failure detection, geographic diversity scoring, and failover path identification
  • Unified Connectivity: Combined IX + Fabric view per ASN per metro — every way to reach a network through Equinix
  • Peering Opportunities: Mutual IX presence discovery — IXes where the customer and a target ASN are both connected. PeeringDB records IX membership, not sessions, so whether the two networks already peer there is not (and cannot be) checked from this data.

Fabric availability is cross-referenced live from the Equinix Fabric service-profile catalog: a target is marked Fabric-reachable at a metro when a service profile whose name identifies that network (curated CloudProviderType matching for known clouds — bridging corporate names like "Amazon.com" to product profiles like "AWS Direct Connect" — otherwise whole-token, brand-distinctive name matching) publishes that metro. It indicates an available private on-ramp, not an existing connection. The cross-reference is best-effort: when the catalog cannot be read, a warning marks Fabric availability as not analyzed rather than reporting false everywhere.

PeeringDB credentials

PeeringDB authentication is an API key (created on peeringdb.com) — a separate credential from the Equinix OAuth client. The key is resolved in this order:

  1. an explicit key — fabric.peeringIntelligence("key") or builder(fabric, "key")
  2. the EquinixConfig.peeringDbApiKey option configured on the client/session
  3. the "PEERINGDB_API_KEY" environment variable
  4. anonymous access (rate-limited by PeeringDB to ~20 requests/minute)

Usage

// Basic presence matrix
PeeringIntelligenceResult result = fabric.peeringIntelligence("your-peeringdb-api-key")
    .addAsn(16509, "AWS")
    .addAsn(8075, "Microsoft")
    .addAsn(15169, "Google")
    .analyze();

System.out.println(result.getPresenceMatrix().toTableString());

// Full analysis with customer context
PeeringIntelligenceResult result = fabric.peeringIntelligence("your-peeringdb-api-key")
    .addAsn(16509, "AWS")
    .addAsn(8075, "Microsoft")
    .customerMetros(MetroCode.DC, MetroCode.DA, MetroCode.SG)
    .customerAsn(65100L)
    .includeCapacity(true)
    .includePolicies(true)
    .includeResiliency(true)
    .analyze();

System.out.println(result.toMarkdown());
